headline: Genetic variation mapped to plasma proteins and aortic stenosis risk
label: Genetic Drivers Of Cardiovascular Risk
summary: Recent genetic and protein profiling studies connect circulating protein networks and non-additive protein genetics to cardiovascular disease risk.
synthesis: The common thread is mapping genetic variation onto circulating protein and transcript abundance to resolve cardiovascular disease risk. Two items operate at the protein level: a causal network inference framework using cis-pQTL instruments across 7523 serum proteins in AGES identified 185 subnetworks linked to future myocardial infarction, while EIR-auto-GP detected dominance and epistasis in UK Biobank plasma pQTLs, replicated in Olink and mass-spectrometry cohorts. The aortic stenosis study extends this to transcriptomics and prediction, reporting a multi-ancestry GWAS of 86,864 cases with 241 autosomal loci, 54 TWAS genes, a polygenic risk score, and CMKLR1 and LTBP4 silencing validation. What is new is the detection of non-additive genetic effects on plasma protein levels alongside causal protein network inference.
